lines.text: &c.-To be brief, in short. वटविटपः &c-it is difficult to see the
propriety of calling the Vata tree ‘a dayita’; probably the poet
refers by dayita’ to गृहस्थाश्रम in which the wife plays a con-
spicuous part. Let the Vata tree be my home i. e. let me
renounce the pleasures of the world and take to a devotee’s life
worshipping S'iva sitting under a Vata tree &c.

r2.note: The Sanskrit quotation is somewhat unclear.

lines.text: Sl. 6. त्रुटित &c.—the worldly ties which proved an obstruc-
tion to them having been snapped. आशीविष—a serpent; fr.
आशी ( a serpent’s fang ) + विष. The derivation more usually
given is fr. आशीस्+विष the comp. being classed under the
पृषोदरादि class. The 2nd l. means ( those blessed persons ) that
do not seek the crooked course of serpentine sensualism. Mr.
Telang takes विषम with आशीविष and says ‘the course of
worldly objects which are like dangerous snakes.’ शरच्चन्द्र &c,—
the night which is delightful on account of the sky being lit
up with the winter moonshine. आभोग—expanse. ( ज्योतिरस्यस्याः
उद्योतः ). चय storing up. शरण—from शृ 9 con. to tear.

r3.note: Several Sanskrit quotations, especially at the end, are difficult to read.

lines.text: Sl. 7. A question to an estranged friend. Once our in-
terests were identical; now you and we have no connection.
What has happened in the meanwhile to estrange us ?
Sl. 8. अमलपटं—of clean texture. पट्टवस्त्रं—silken cloth.
कदशनं—By Pán. VI. 3. 101. ( see com. ) कद् is substituted for
कु in a Tat. when the latter member begins with a vowel; coarse
food. व्यक्त &c.—The idea is—A man who has renounced the
world and devoted himself to the service of God entirely is
indifferent to all such things as are mentioned in the s'loka.
Sl. 9. स्मर &c.—Love is often described as blinding men’s
eyes, पटुतर &c.—विवेक is here called collyrium because it
sharpens, restores, or preserves the sight of the mind. समी-
भूता—Made even, rectified, corrected. Râmarshi explains it by
निर्विकल्पा. Mr. Telang takes it to mean ‘looking on all things
alike.’

r6.note: The first Sanskrit quotation on line 2 is unclear.

lines.text: Sl. 10. मान haughtiness. विविक्त—lonely, solitary; p. p. of
विच् with वि. यमिनाम्—of those who restrain their minds ).

r7.note: The Sanskrit root and punctuation at the end are obscured.
